entry.title: Correction: 2026-09-01
entry.summary: On 55 published day pages from 2026-09-01 to 2026-11-19 the party totals that shares were printed against were too small. Democrats: 257 where the refreshed roster has 258 on 2026-09-01 and 259 from 2026-09-02. Republicans: 269 where it has 271 on the 12 pages from 2026-11-04 to 2026-11-19. No Republican total printed before 2026-11-04 changes (the 2026-11-03 audit changes by one, but that page prints no total). These pages were assembled before 2026-11-21 and count voting members only, so they are compared with the refreshed roster's voting members; the five offices involved are all voting members. Each printed share was therefore slightly overstated. Computed over all 983 shares printed on those 55 pages, the largest difference is 0.08 percentage points (28 of 257, printed 10.9 percent, is 10.8 percent of 259, Democrats, 2026-09-11); 198 shares change in their printed decimal, none by more than 0.1 points. The same totals appear as counts, without a percentage, on 516 phrase pages whose peak day falls in the window. No ranking, threshold or selection used these totals, so no phrase or Daily Line changes.

entry.title: Correction: 2025-01-03
entry.summary: Since the ledger's first build, any phrase used in 2 of those 31 or 36 statements was removed from the whole ledger, whatever its share among the roughly 75,000 statements of the 119th Congress. Rebuilt from the raw mirror through 2026-07-09, 89 phrases were removed this way (27 by the Democratic stratum, 63 by the Republican, one by both); each reached the three-office floor on at least one day, 82 of them for Democrats and 81 for Republicans. They are generic phrases such as "look forward to working with" and "house of representatives". None has a phrase page or a phrase-evidence entry. None would have entered the repeated-phrase table of 2026-06-30, the only published day in the rebuilt window on which any of them reached the floor (that table's smallest row held 9 offices; the largest restored phrase held 5). Two of them ("the house of representatives", "look forward to working") appear as Daily Line talking-point labels on four published days (2026-07-20, 07-21, 11-04, 11-10); those come from the claim-clustering path, which never read this cap, and do not change. The instrument fingerprint attested a setting the instrument did not apply.

entry.title: Correction: 2025-01-03
entry.summary: Wherever a page printed a count of offices over a party's eligible offices (for example "40 of 257"), the count could include up to three nonvoting offices that the total left out: three Democratic and three Republican delegates are seated. A share could be overstated by at most three offices, a little over one percentage point. Measured from 2025-01-03 to 2026-07-09, a delegate was in the count on 328 of 550 Democratic party-days and 276 of 545 Republican party-days, an average of 0.89 Democratic and 0.66 Republican offices a day. No ranking, threshold or selection used the share, so no phrase, Daily Line or award changes.

entry.title: Correction: 2026-10-28
entry.summary: The fourteen daily records from 2026-10-28 through 2026-11-10, which include Election Day and the week after it, were not measured as they happened. They were assembled on 2026-11-11 from the same public source record, with the same prompts, thresholds and code the freeze had locked. Four things about them differ from an ordinary day. First, none of the fourteen was posted to Bluesky; they are site-only by ruling. Second, 2026-11-03 was published by an explicit repair run that bypasses the readiness gate: it held 25 statements, at most about 31 percent of its same-weekday baseline, a share the gate would have held back and force-finalized with a flag. Third, the records from 2026-10-28 through 2026-11-09 lack the legacy metrics block the collect stage normally writes; that block is not shown on any page. Fourth, the unpublished silence boards for 2026-10-28 through 2026-11-04 were not built. Thirteen of the assemble manifests record a manual run; the manifest for 2026-11-05 records a scheduled run on 2026-11-11.

entry.title: Correction: 2026-07-09
entry.summary: Three published phrase pages claimed the citation quorum on two source units rather than three. Pages 007eacff261c652d (airport to rehabilitate), 2dc5adb851e6e29d (to deliver for our), and e0b16e162cdabc40 (fought to ensure) each showed grounded_units 3, the exact floor, and two of the three receipts on each page were the same 2026-07-09 Nevada airports announcement, published by the Cortez Masto office and the Rosen office with the name order swapped. Measured similarity between the two texts was 0.647 against a near-duplicate bar of 0.72. Every receipt on those pages is a real, verified, correctly quoted source; the defect is the count, which credited one announcement twice and so let three pages rest on two independent offices. Across the 540 published evidence records, 89 carried an uncollapsed same-day cosigned pair and the other 86 remain above the quorum after the collapse. No composite claim, no posted thread, and no cross-party number is affected.

entry.title: Correction: 2026-07-25
entry.summary: The published instrument fingerprint misdescribed the live measurement instrument. Its method-version registry attested document-families-v1 and surface-eligibility-v2 while the running modules were at document-families-v2 and surface-eligibility-v3, and its schema-version registry attested corrections schema 2 while the running schema was 3. The registry held hand-copied version strings rather than reading them from the owning modules, so it went stale when later work advanced those modules. The fingerprint also keyed code identity on the repository commit, which data commits move, so one measurement could carry a different identity on its day record than on its post manifest. The 2026-07-25 day record and post manifest are the committed instances. Every number and every citation on those surfaces was correct. The defect was in how the instrument described itself, not in any measurement.

entry.title: Correction: 2026-07-15 through 2026-07-23
entry.summary: Some daily composite claims attached the size of a transitively connected topic cluster to a verbatim phrase carried by only part of that cluster, while the three displayed receipts could support a different phrase from the same cluster. The composite quote appeared in all three receipts in 2 of 38 stored blocks and in none of them in 14 of 38. The rendered label was absent from at least one receipt in 28 of 63 blocks. The two complete misses were the Democratic block on 2026-07-15 and the Republican block on 2026-07-22. The same code and the same correction apply to both parties.

entry.title: Correction: 2026-07-20
entry.summary: A phrase containing the name of a private individual — a person named in members' statements about a fatal law-enforcement incident — appeared in the synchronized-phrase table on that day's page, on the phrases index, and on the home page. OnScript measures elected officials' public statements and does not rank or page private citizens, regardless of how newsworthy the underlying event is. A different name-window form of the same name was already withheld, but the suppression list did not carry every window an n-gram can slide across, so this form was not matched. Every citation involved was valid and every number was correct — the citation verifier has no opinion about privacy, by construction, so no receipts audit could have caught this.

entry.title: Correction: 2 days (2026-07-12, 2026-07-18)
entry.summary: The composite Daily Lines and talking points for two already-published days went MISSING from this site. The daily collection run rewrites the day record it is working on, and when it landed on a day that had already been published it overwrote that day's composite half with nothing — deleting the two party composites, their talking points, and the day's cross-party phrase pairings. Nothing published was WRONG: no number changed, no citation broke, and the underlying record of what members actually said was never touched. Content that had been published simply stopped being there, and one day's page went on displaying composites whose backing data had been removed. Because every surviving number stayed correct, no receipts audit or citation check could have surfaced this — it is an absence, and the verifier has no opinion about absence. It was found by the pre-launch health review, before this site had an audience.

entry.title: Correction: 7 days (2026-06-30…2026-07-17)
entry.summary: Some daily talking points were bound by a connective or attribution phrase rather than a message — e.g. “into the trump administration’s” or “democratic colleagues in demanding the”. Each such key is string-valid (every cited statement contains it verbatim, which is why they clustered) and cleared the >=3 quorum, but the shared span is grammar, not a shared message, so the receipts pointed at unrelated topics. The citation verifier checks verbatim-ness, quorum and attribution — not whether the shared span is a message — so no receipts audit could have caught it. Flagged talking points: 19 across 7 day(s), categorized by reason (18 incomplete syntactic span, 1 attribution frame), both parties (15 D / 4 R — the gate is party-blind; the skew tracks the caucus).
